main_topics.reason: The user came because of daily nausea three weeks into Ozempic and the topic ran through most of the conversation.
The user directly asked whether it was safe to stop for some days, and said they were almost stopping that day.
The user feared worse nausea at the next dose increase and was relieved to learn they can ask to delay it.
The user described fried food, meat and evening meals worsening nausea and accepted the bot's meal tips.
The user asked when the nausea would be not normal and need fast medical help, and checked themselves against the signs.
The user asked whether the medication was working and shared morning readings over a couple of turns.
The user decided to raise the nausea and dose pace with the doctor, and the bot gave wording for it.
The user mentioned once that their wife said they should stop, as background to the question.

output.summary: A user three weeks into Ozempic for diabetes had daily nausea and asked whether to stop. The bot explained the side effect, gave meal tips, advised against stopping without the doctor, explained the dose increase can be delayed, listed warning signs and reviewed morning sugar readings. The user said they felt calmer and planned to keep the meal changes, check sugar more and talk to the doctor before the dose goes up. No urgent symptoms or bot-claimed actions occurred.
